# WP1-a: physics visibility of Sherlock attacks

Reconstructed grid (pandapower CIGRE MV with all DER, 32 switches, transformer parameters and tap changer identified from data, `rules/sherlock_grid_params.json`). Inputs taken from the IPAL state that the control center sees (vantage n302): load, DER and storage P and Q, connection, switch and tap states, external grid voltage. Residual = max abs difference between reported and recomputed bus voltages, line P (from end) and transformer P (HV). Every 1th record of the 1 Hz state; power flows by the cached fast solver (validated against runpp). Attack window = [start, recovery].

Two detectors, both calibrated on train only (no attacks), fixed before looking at test:

- D0: alarm when a residual exceeds 1.2 x its train maximum.
- D1: alarm when a residual stays above theta = 2.0 x its train 99.9th percentile for at least L consecutive records, L = ceil(1.5 x longest train run above theta), at least 3.

Reading: a physics-consistency rule (and therefore any rule the physics oracle certifies) can only catch attacks that make the telemetry physically inconsistent. Attacks that change the real grid through valid commands keep the telemetry consistent and need state-transition or context rules instead.
